chapter_title: Chương 276: Trần Quý Lương Mua Nhà

segments.title: Chương 276: Trần Quý Lương Mua Nhà
segments.content:
Bian Guanyue’s bath caused a delay, and the hotel had already cleared away the breakfast buffet.

The three of them decided to just check out.

It was only at checkout that they discovered three rooms had been booked.

Bian Guanyue pouted, feeling a little better inside.

They strolled along the street and randomly picked a breakfast shop.

They ordered some millet porridge, lamb offal soup, soy milk, steamed buns, fried dough sticks, and so on. Last night, they were so focused on drinking and eating dishes that they didn't have any staples, so now they were all a bit hungry.

Chen Guiliang brought up the main topic: "Are you really going to apply for the master's program at the Central Conservatory of Music?"

"Not necessarily the Central Conservatory," Bian Guanyue said. "Tsinghua or Peking University would be fine too, but I'm afraid their graduate programs are too hard to get into."

Chen Guiliang asked, "What's the difference in admission standards among these three?"

Bian Guanyue said, "I asked around a bit. The Central Conservatory is more in-depth and specialized, focusing on music itself. The vocal lessons I took before, plus the folk music I learned over the last two or three school breaks, would all be useful. Tsinghua and Peking University, on the other hand, place more emphasis on general academic subjects, theory, critical thinking, and academic writing skills."

Chen Guiliang thought for a moment. "Is it possible that, for you, the Central Conservatory's master's program is actually harder to get into?"

Bian Guanyue thought it over carefully.

Tao Xue had already finished a steamed bun by the time Bian Guanyue nodded and said, "It's possible."

Chen Guiliang helped her analyze it: "The Central Conservatory focuses more on musical ability. The top music majors from all over the country might apply there. But the vocal lessons you took in junior and senior high were very basic, nowhere near the level of those professional students. If you apply to Tsinghua or Peking, however, the little bit of musical knowledge you have would be just enough to meet their requirements. Before graduating from your undergrad, you just need to focus on your general academic subjects."

The more Bian Guanyue thought about it, the more sense it made. "Then I'll try for Tsinghua or Peking."

Actually, there was something Chen Guiliang hadn't said. If Bian Guanyue were to apply for Peking University's master's program, he could help her contact a professor in advance.

Of course, Bian Guanyue's academic and professional abilities would have to be up to par. After all, Peking University wasn't owned by Chen Guiliang.

Chen Guiliang wasn't idle. While dipping a fried dough stick into his soy milk, he started calling professors he knew.

After a few calls, he got a general idea of the situation.

Chen Guiliang put down his phone and said, "At Peking University's School of Arts, Professor Dong is the most suitable for you. He specializes in wind instruments and traditional opera research. His representative work is an adaptation of 'Three Variations on the Yangguan Theme.'"

"Are you going to help me pull some strings?" Bian Guanyue said with a smile.

Chen Guiliang said, "I'm just helping you gather some information. Don't you visit old folk artists during your winter and summer breaks? Before your graduate school interview, decide on a research topic related to traditional music. If the topic is novel and interesting, you'll have a high chance of being admitted even without my help."

"When mentors at Peking University's School of Arts recruit graduate students, that's what they value most. Because 99% of students who interview don't have a clear research topic, and haven't even thought about what they want to research. If you can present a topic, it will make a fantastic impression on the mentors."

Bian Guanyue said happily, "I understand."

When it came to solving practical problems, so-called connections didn't necessarily have to be used in illicit ways.

Information was the most important thing!

Especially when the internet wasn't yet well-developed, the vast majority of people failed simply due to a lack of information.

Tao Xue was still chewing on her steamed bun, seemingly carefree, but a storm of thoughts was brewing in her mind. She felt like a child sitting next to her senior and senior sister as they discussed serious matters.

Does Senior like career-oriented girls? Hmm, maybe not career-oriented, but someone who has her own things to do.

What can I do?

Oh dear, I don't even know myself. This question is such a headache.

She had accidentally eaten three meat buns and, touching her stomach, still didn't feel very full. She noticed that Bian Guanyue had barely eaten anything before putting down her chopsticks, appearing more like a lady from a distinguished family than she did.

Tao Xue's eyes darted around until she finally found her own strong suit.

Hmph, Senior Sister's chest isn't as big as mine. It must be because she doesn't eat enough!

They took a walk to digest after the meal. It was actually almost noon.

The atmosphere among the three was a bit delicate, and they all felt it was pointless to keep walking. Tao Xue took the initiative to say she had to go back to school, and Bian Guanyue also said it was time for her to head back.

Chen Guiliang decided to go to his company to get his car and drive them back to campus himself.

Minzu University of China was just a short drive away. Tao Xue got out of the car and waved. "Goodbye, Senior! Goodbye, Senior Sister!"

She was as cheerful as ever, as if her mood hadn't been affected at all.

As if!

After Chen Guiliang and Bian Guanyue waved goodbye, Tao Xue turned toward the school gate, pouting and sulking with her back to them.

Chen Guiliang continued driving.

They hadn't gone far when Bian Guanyue said, "You're going the wrong way. You shouldn't have turned here."

Chen Guiliang said, "I'm taking you to look at an apartment."

"Look at an apartment?" Bian Guanyue was confused.

How could Chen Guiliang not know that the beautiful Miss Bian had been feeling wronged for the past two days? He had to cheer her up.

Chen Guiliang smiled. "The property deed will have both our names on it."

Bian Guanyue's lips curled into a smile when she heard that. "I'm not going to marry you."

Chen Guiliang said, "We can still buy it without being married. We'll consider it a joint property investment."

"Then I'll have to contribute some... All my remaining money, aside from living expenses, I lent to my cousin to start a factory," Bian Guanyue's voice grew softer.

Chen Guiliang said, "No problem, I'll consider half of the purchase price a loan to you."

Bian Guanyue said, "Then I'll have to write an IOU and pay you back with interest according to the bank loan rate."

"Why would we need an IOU between us? When I started my company, you lent me money without one," Chen Guiliang said.

Bian Guanyue didn't say anything more. She turned her face to look at the scenery outside the car window, but she couldn't suppress the smile on her face.

She wasn't coveting the apartment; the important thing was having both their names on the deed.

Just like a married couple.

Chen Guiliang thought this was a pretty good idea. In the future, he could also buy a house with Tao Xue and put both their names on it.

Sigh, how am I becoming more and more of a scumbag?

Chen Guiliang, oh Chen Guiliang, you can't keep going on like this.

An apartment in Huaqing Jiayuan was, of course, the first choice, but the sales office there had closed down in 2004. Now, they could only buy a pre-owned one.

He drove to Huaqing Jiayuan and randomly entered a real estate agency.

A salesperson immediately came to greet them, then exclaimed in surprise, "Mr. Chen... no, CEO Chen! Please, have a seat. I'll get you... would you like tea or coffee?"

This place was not far from Zhongguancun, and especially close to Tsinghua Science Park. Many founders and executives of IT companies came here to buy apartments.

The salespeople paid special attention to the internet industry, especially Beijing's IT companies.

How could they not recognize Chen Guiliang when they read internet news every day?

"Tea."

"Just plain water is fine."

Half the real estate agency was in an uproar. Many employees came over to see what was happening, but they were quickly shooed back by the company owner.

The owner came to serve them personally, while the commission for this sale would go to the person from just now.

The owner asked eagerly, "CEO Chen, what size are you looking for? Which residential complex? Do you have any requirements for the location and floor?"

Chen Guiliang asked, "What's the largest unit in Huaqing Jiayuan?"

The owner said, "Huaqing Jiayuan was built quite a while ago. Even the third phase opened in 2000. Compact apartments were popular back then. One-bedrooms make up 25%, small two-bedrooms 40%, and standard two-bedrooms 20%. These are all under 100 square meters."

"Three-bedroom units of 100 square meters or more make up 15%, with the largest being 130 square meters. However, there are also top-floor duplexes, which are less than 1% of the total, with the smallest being 150 square meters and the largest 180."

"For someone of CEO Chen's status, you'd surely be choosing between the three-bedrooms and the top-floor duplexes. We have seven or eight of those listed, some of them never even renovated."

Chen Guiliang asked, "Show me the top-floor duplexes."

The owner said, "We only have one top-floor duplex listed. But the owner has very strict requirements. The full payment must be made before the end of the year. As long as the full payment can be made by year's end, the owner is willing to compromise a little on the price."

"Is the owner in a hurry to go abroad?" Chen Guiliang asked.

The owner smiled. "CEO Chen most likely knows the owner. But the information must be kept confidential. If CEO Chen is interested in buying, I can call the owner right now."
